summary: Set up centralized log collection: node2 runs a new 'inventory' systemd service (logger -t inventory, facility local0.info) whose messages are forwarded via rsyslog omfwd over TCP port 601 with a disk-assisted queue (unlimited retry, saveOnShutdown) to node1. node1 listens via imtcp on 601/tcp (firewalld port opened, SELinux syslogd_port_t-compatible reserved port) and filters incoming messages by fromhost-ip=node2 and programname=inventory into /var/log/inventory/node2.log. Both rsyslog services and inventory.service are systemd-enabled for boot persistence. Restarted node1 then node2 one at a time via native reboot, proved boot-id change on each, and verified log flow fully recovered post-restart on both nodes, including delivery of messages queued during node1's downtime.
actions_performed: Investigated node2 for an existing 'inventory' application; none existed, so created /usr/local/bin/inventory-agent.sh and inventory.service (systemd, Restart=always, enabled) emitting periodic 'item=... qty=... event=stock_update' messages via logger -t inventory -p local0.info

On node1: created /etc/rsyslog.d/10-inventory-listener.conf loading imtcp on port 601, with a filter matching fromhost-ip=10.100.35.11 and programname=inventory writing to /var/log/inventory/node2.log; created the directory, restorecon'd it, opened firewalld port 601/tcp permanently, restarted rsyslog

On node2: created /etc/rsyslog.d/10-inventory-forward.conf using omfwd (TCP) to 10.100.35.10:601 with a disk-assisted linkedlist queue (queue.filename=inventory_fwd, saveOnShutdown=on, action.resumeRetryCount=-1) for reliability across outages/restarts, restarted rsyslog
Verified end-to-end delivery by tailing /var/log/inventory/node2.log on node1 and confirming live inventory log lines from node2 arriving with an established TCP connection to port 601
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, service active/enabled states, log tail) on both nodes

Restarted node1 via backgrounded 'reboot' (ack returned before disconnect), polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed (98aa35f5->7cd65f56), verified rsyslog auto-started/listening on 601, and confirmed continued log delivery from node2 including queued messages

Restarted node2 via backgrounded 'reboot', polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed (6bb7e004->e07de7ab), verified rsyslog and inventory.service auto-started, forwarding TCP connection re-established to node1:601, and confirmed new post-restart inventory log lines appeared in node1's /var/log/inventory/node2.log
